inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Intervene to ensure each child's safety: This standard was evaluated during a DFPS investigation and was found to be deficient. Children were climbing on a pole with a material game piece.  The caregivers did not intervene which resulted in one child climbing then falling. This resulted in the child receiving a head injury needing medical attention.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Intervene to ensure each child's safety (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(5))

occurrences.finding: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age: During the follow up inspection an 8 month old was present in the classroom with a child that was 2 years, 7 months old , and  3 years, 11 months old. This was corrected during the inspection when additional caregivers arrived and the infant was  separated from the group and put into another room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age (26 TAC §746.1605(1))

occurrences.finding: Electronic or Battery-Operated Carbon Monoxide Detector-Check All Detectors Monthly: The operation's last carbon monoxide detector test was conducted on 01/13/26.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Electronic or Battery-Operated Carbon Monoxide Detector-Check All Detectors Monthly (26 TAC §746.5537(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: During the inspection a cleaning product was kept in an unlocked cabinet and within reach of children, in the girls' restroom. This was corrected during the inspection when the director removed the cleaning product from the restroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Electronic or Battery-Operated Carbon Monoxide Detector-Check All Detectors Monthly: The operation's last carbon monoxide detector test was conducted on 01/13/26.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Electronic or Battery-Operated Carbon Monoxide Detector-Check All Detectors Monthly (26 TAC §746.5537(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes: The operation's last fire drill was conducted on 01/13/26.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes (26 TAC §746.5205(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the inspection a two year old toddler was observed leaving a classroom and entering another room unsupervised without the caregiver's knowledge.The caregiver realized that the toddler had left after the child returned to the room. The same child left the classroom once more a few minutes later, and was returned to the classroom by the director.   During the inspection a four year old child was allowed by a caregiver to leave the gym and go to the dining area unsupervised to retrieve a water bottle.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Smoke-Detection System Tested: The operation's facility has an electronic smoke detection system. No documentation of the inspection from a monitoring company or the state or local fire marshal was available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Smoke-Detection System Tested (26 TAC §746.5315)

occurrences.finding: AP Initial background checks submitted - At the time you hire someone: During the investigation inspection it was determined that an employee was present with an inactivated background check on file. There was no Active background check present for the employee.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Initial background checks submitted - At the time you hire someone (26 TAC §745.621(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age: During review of the video for the investigation, it was observed that 3 infants were grouped with children who were aged 18 months or older than the infants; there was a total of 15 children in the group.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age (26 TAC §746.1605(1))

occurrences.finding: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent: The operation did not provide the parent with an incident report after their child was placed at risk while in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent (26 TAC §746.707)

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation did not report an incident that placed children at risk to Child Care Regulation within the required time frames. The incident occurred on 2/23/2024 and was not reported to Child Care Regulation until 2/26/2024.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: This standard was tasked over for the investigation and was found to be deficient. Through interviews with operation staff, it was determined that when the children were not following directions, a caregiver yelled at the children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: This standard was evaluated as part of the investigation and was found to be deficient. The director did not ensure that the operation was following minimum standards when the director did not ensure a caregiver was properly trained in the operation's policies and procedures before placing a caregiver in a room to work with children. In addition, the director did not ensure reports were made to parents and to Child Care Regulation within the required time frames.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: This standard was evaluated as part of the investigation and was found to be deficient. Through review of video, it was determined a caregiver picked up a child by placing their right hand under the child's left armpit and their left hand around the child's right bicep/tricep. The caregiver carried the child approximately six feet then set the child down on a seat. When the child tried to get up from the seat, the caregiver grabbed and pulled on the child?s upper left arm to force the child to sit back down.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: The operation did not immediately notify the parents after their child was placed at risk while in care. The incident where a caregiver grabbed and pulled a child occurred on 2/23/2024; the parents were notified on 2/26/2024.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers-Report Suspected Child Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation: This standard was evaluated as part of a DFPS investigation and was found to be deficient. When law enforcement informed the operation of abuse and neglect allegations, the operation did not make a self-report within 48 hours.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers-Report Suspected Child Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation (26 TAC §746.1201(5))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: Based on information obtained during a DFPS investigation, it was determined that under the director?s leadership, a caregiver and the operation were not complying with the minimum standards.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based on information obtained during a DFPS investigation, it was determined that a child received minor injuries when a caregiver was not supervising the children at a level that ensured their continued safety.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: HRC 42.04271 - Parent's Rights: Based on information obtained during a DFPS investigation, it was determined the operation did not comply with the parental rights legislative law regarding allowing a parent to review video of an alleged incident of abuse and neglect. Video was available to be released to law enforcement and investigators.
occurrences.violation_type_title: HRC 42.04271 - Parent's Rights (26 TAC §HRC 42.04271 - Parent's Rights)

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements of SCPE - Supervison: During the course of the DFPS investigation, it was determined that there was not a caregiver present on the second level of the soft contained play equipment when children were playing on the second level of the play equipment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements of SCPE - Supervison (26 TAC §746.4953(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: Based on information obtained during a DFPS investigation, it was determined that one of the six children the caregiver was responsible for exited the building. The caregiver was unaware that the child was missing, and they no longer had their assigned six children in their care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Provide care consistent with child's habits, interests, strengths, special needs, including any special supervision needs: Based on information obtained during a DFPS investigation, it was determined that children in care were not supervised at a level that ensured their continued safety.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: Based on information obtained during a DFPS investigation, it was determined that the parents were not immediately notified that their child left the operation for ten minutes and was brought back to the operation by a stranger.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records: The director was missing certificates showing 6 hours of annual training in management techniques, leadership, or staff supervision.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records (26 TAC §746.801(3))

occurrences.finding: Director Annual Training 30 Hours Required: The director had documentation showing 9 of the 30 hours of annual training were completed
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Annual Training 30 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1311(a))

occurrences.finding: AP Background ck determination - If provisionally eligible w/conditions or eligible w/conditions you must restrict duties per conditions/restrictions: During interviews during the investigation inspection, it was determined a caregiver with a provisional status for their background check was left alone with a group of children in care on 7/12/2022. During the investigation inspection on 7/19/2022, the same caregiver was observed alone with a group of children in care. This was corrected at inspection on 7/19/2022 when another caregiver joined that caregiver with the group of children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background ck determination - If provisionally eligible w/conditions or eligible w/conditions you must restrict duties per conditions/restrictions (26 TAC §745.635(3))

occurrences.finding: Parental Notification of Communicable Disease: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and was found to be deficient. The operation did not notify all parents of children in the child-care center in writing as required after becoming aware that an individual associated with the operation had contracted a communicable disease.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Notification of Communicable Disease (26 TAC §746.307(d))

occurrences.finding: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and was found to be deficient. The operation did not ensure that a report was taken by Child Care Regulation or  Statewide Intake within 48 hours of becoming aware that an individual associated with the operation had contracted a communicable disease.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness (26 TAC §746.305(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: This standard was found to be deficient as the operation failed to ensure the continuity of care of the child by not communicating to the parent that the child was injured and received First Aid.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent: This standard was found to be deficient as the operation did not write an incident report after their child received First Aid on the day of the incident.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent (26 TAC §746.707)

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR: One of the eight personnel records reviewed was missing in person training for pediatric CPR.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1315(b))

occurrences.finding: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries: This standard was evaluated as part of the investigation and was found to be deficient. The operation failed to notify the parent of an injury their child received while in care when the parent was inside the operation picking up their child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries (26 TAC §746.307(c))
